title: Understanding N-grams
text: Think about how N-grams work. They capture sequences of letters, but do they consider the biological significance of codons?

title: Non-consecutive Segments
text: Consider how N-grams might treat sequences that aren't directly next to each other. How might this affect the interpretation of DNA sequences?

title: Meaningless Segments
text: Think about the biological meaning of single letters or pairs of letters in DNA. How does this relate to the concept of codons?

title: Overlapping Segments
text: How does the N-gram model handle overlapping sequences? Consider the sequence ATGCA. What overlapping segments would be captured?

hintAnswer: Yes, it might capture segments like TGG from GGTT.
title: Wrap-around Segments
text: Does the N-gram model consider the end of a sequence as connected to the beginning? What might this imply for DNA sequences?
choices: Yes, it might capture segments like TGG from GGTT.
No, it only considers linear sequences.
Yes, but only for sequences longer than $$3$$ letters.
No, it treats each sequence independently.
